title: Emrys and the Tide
premise: Orsen Vane inherited Vane Vineyard along with a mountain of debt, saved only by a lucrative career as a ghostwritten romance novelist whose anonymous letters to readers became a cult phenomenon. When Emrys Hale—the reader whose decade of letters Orsen secretly answered as 'the Vane Voice'—moves into the cottage next door to research the letters' author, Orsen hides his identity while falling for the one person who knows his written heart. As harvest approaches and Emrys closes in on the truth, Orsen must choose between selling his anonymity to a publisher who wants the letters and risking everything to claim them—and Emrys—publicly. He chooses Emrys, reading his final letter aloud at the harvest festival, and they rebuild the vineyard together.
about_author: Bram Winterbourne is the pen name of a former wine-country journalist who spent years listening to vintners talk about the crops that broke them and the people who saved them. They write romances about stubborn people and stubborn land, usually from a porch with a view of something ripening.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He surveys the failing vineyard, the foreclosure notices, and the one asset he guards: his secret career ghostwriting the 'Vane Letters,' anonymous missives that readers treasure. A letter arrives announcing that the letters' most devoted correspondent has moved to the valley. Beat: weary resignation shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: The Cottage Next Door
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys Hale, a literary archivist, arrives with boxes of the letters he's collected for ten years, determined to unmask the author before the publisher's deadline. He meets his gruff neighbor over a collapsed fence and finds him oddly familiar. Beat: hopeful curiosity meeting a closed door.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Forced into proximity repairing the fence and sharing tools, Orsen discovers Emrys quotes the letters from memory—his own words, tender and unguarded. Orsen lies about knowing them well and hates how easily it comes. Beat: the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Letters Knew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys interviews valley locals about the letters, learning the author answered readers' private griefs with uncanny precision. Orsen deflects with wine and work, but Emrys notices the man's silences match the letters' pauses. Beat: suspicion blooming into fascination.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A late frost threatens the vines; Orsen and Emrys work through the night lighting fires between rows. Exhausted and honest, Orsen almost confesses, then retreats when Emrys mentions the reward the publisher offers for the author's name. Beat: warmth snatched back at the edge of trust.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys finds a draft letter in Orsen's study—handwriting matching the Vane Letters—and says nothing, testing him instead with a fabricated detail. Orsen corrects it instinctively. Both know; neither speaks. Beat: charged, dangerous intimacy.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Harvest begins; Emrys stays to help, and the found-family thread widens as neighbors, field hands, and Emrys become the crew Orsen never let himself need. They kiss among the rows. Orsen still hasn't said the truth aloud. Beat: joy with a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Sold
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The publisher, tipped by a rival, announces the letters' author will be revealed at the harvest festival—with or without consent. Emrys realizes Orsen's silence was protection, not deception, and confronts him. Orsen, humiliated, pushes him away. Beat: betrayal, heartbreak, and the truth finally spoken too late.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen nearly signs the publisher's contract, trading anonymity for the money that saves the vineyard. Instead, he writes one final letter—to Emrys—and decides to read it himself at the festival, publicly claiming a decade of tenderness. Beat: the choice, made at cost.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the festival, Orsen reads the last letter aloud, naming Emrys before the crowd and the publisher alike. The vineyard's future is uncertain but shared; the community rallies around its reluctant author. Emrys answers with a letter of his own. Beat: love claimed in the open, inheritance redefined.
